Chief Justice Roberts moves oldest active federal judge's fitness investigation to 11th Circuit

By Victor Li

October 7, 2026, 11:57 am CDT

  •  
  •  
  •  
  • Email
  • Print

Judge Pauline Newman, now age 99, of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit in May 2023. (Photo by Bill O’Leary/The Washington Post via Getty Images)

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:40
Instaread

Judge Pauline Newman of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit has long argued that the investigation into her fitness should be handled by a neutral circuit, rather than her colleagues.

According to Law360, Newman will get her wish. On Tuesday, the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals at Atlanta revealed that Chief Justice John Roberts had transferred the matter to the appeals court Aug. 19. According to Law360, 11th Circuit Chief Judge William H. Pryor Jr. made the order public at Newman’s request and will consider releasing more filings as the matter proceeds.

Newman’s argument has been that the fitness investigations must include district and circuit judges from that region. The Federal Circuit has only its own judges, so Newman’s colleagues are effectively investigating one of their own—something that Newman claims is a conflict of interest.

Newman, age 99, has been suspended since 2023 after refusing to undergo medical testing on terms set by the Federal Circuit’s judicial council. The suspension has been renewed twice.

The latest one lapsed in late August, though her lawyers at the New Civil Liberties Alliance, a nonprofit public interest law firm, said her status hasn’t changed, Law360 reports.

Before that, Newman’s appeal was dismissed by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit in August 2025. The U.S. Supreme Court then declined to hear her case in June.

The New Civil Liberties Alliance told Law360 in a statement that it welcomed the transfer.
